material_facts: Historical Section 42 breaches and pending appeal require scrutiny.

CAP.name: Incremental capital efficiency
material_facts: Incremental capital proxy rises 83.7711 versus NOPAT 4.19745, a weak 5.01% diagnostic.

CAP.contrary_fact_or_search: Historical profit margins are attractive; the crude diagnostic is not sufficient to prove a below-cost cohort return either.
CAP.rationale: NS because attribution is unresolved, not neutral and not a disguised high-ROCE score. Need comparable gross/net fee economics and collection-adjusted project/software capital cohorts.

CASH.name: Operating cash realization
material_facts: FY23–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is negative 0.22384; FY25 and FY26 CFO each below minus 9 crore.
Receivables reached 86.5647 with 9.6508 over one year; bad-debt expense rose to 1.6244.
CASH.contrary_fact_or_search: FY24 CFO was positive and FY25 cheques did subsequently clear; management reports some later AR recovery.
CASH.rationale: Persistent poor cash conversion across a profitable period supports severe weakness. It triggers the GQS cap of 5, but does not itself prove false sales.

BAL.name: Funding resilience

BAL.contrary_fact_or_search: IPO funding and June deployment are real; FY25 cheques realized and subsequent recoveries may improve October resources.

EXEC.contrary_fact_or_search: Actual developer mandate wins and partial collection progress are positive.
EXEC.rationale: Mixed operating delivery, not a long record of verified promises met. Funding risk is scored elsewhere.

material_facts: FY26 EBIT rose to 27.2655 and PAT 19.2104; most profit is operating, not other income.

EARN.rationale: Mixed but substantially operating earnings growth. Software capitalization and dilution constrain confidence; cash realization is handled in CASH, not charged again here.

Funded rescue reverse test reaches the 15% hurdle around 3.94% constant growth, but relies on 25% EBIT, better collections and financing.
P.contrary_fact_or_search: Without current cash feasibility, cheap reported earnings and book value may not be realizable.
P.rationale: Fair-execution price rather than demonstrably conservative opportunity: the low multiple is balanced by funding/collection assumptions. No R score is implied by this bounded price diagnostic.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Justo Realfintech is a real-estate sales and marketing services company, not a lender. Its profitable developer mandates, repeat relationships and relatively low earnings multiple are the positive case. The decisive contrary evidence is that accounting profit has not become operating cash: FY23–26 cumulative CFO was minus ₹12.57 crore against ₹56.17 crore PAT. At the ₹82.90 secondary observation, it is a conditional value/collection-recovery candidate, not a demonstrated growth compounder. The conclusion is Hold—unresolved, not an assertion of fraud or default. Current accessible funding and executable SME liquidity must be established before an ordinary return or investment ranking is defensible. Realization of FY26 cheques, collection discipline and actual incremental returns could change that assessment; a lower price alone cannot settle those questions.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The canonical integer factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 5 and L NS. Missingness is not a neutral five and is not silently renormalized. BQS has 80% scored coverage, known contribution 3.48 and missing-factor bounds 3.68–5.48, with no point score. GQS has 85% coverage, known contribution 3.75 and raw bounds 3.90–5.25. Persistent CASH 2 caps a completed GQS at 5, making the bounded range 3.90–5.00, not a completed score.

IAS uses the final unrounded BQS as Q, not a substitute quality score. It has 30% primitive coverage and known contribution 1.10. Independent 1–10 missing bounds are 1.80–8.10; propagating the narrower BQS bounds gives 2.47–6.97. These are uncertainty bounds, not valuations or ranked estimates. All three composites remain NS and all ranking flags are false. Each factor below lists at least two material observations, contrary evidence, confidence and evidence links. Cash weakness is not repeatedly used to lower every factor: CASH addresses realization, BAL remains unresolved, D captures stress loss, and EARN addresses profit source and dilution.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The economic customer is principally a property developer engaging Justo to organize sales, marketing support and channel-partner distribution. FY26 consulting/support revenue was ₹89.9866 crore, home-loan brokerage ₹1.7960 crore and fundraising fees nil, totaling ₹91.7826 crore. A buyer mortgage arranged is not an issuer loan asset; no lender capital-adequacy or credit-book valuation is imposed. Similarly, property GMV belongs to developer inventory, not issuer turnover. The August announcement of ₹300 crore sourcing mandates is therefore an inventory opportunity, not ₹300 crore of revenue or a firm fee order book.

Under the direct/gross model, the developer pays Justo and Justo expenses a channel-partner fee. Under the net model, the developer pays that fee directly, so identical underlying property activity can yield different reported revenue. Developer-funded project marketing does not mean Justo has no salary, administrative, lead or technology costs. Fees depend on sales milestones and collection terms, with meaningful developer credit exposure. FY25 was heavily Pune/Mumbai concentrated; current concentration is missing. No separately identified buyer escrow/customer-fund liability was located, but that does not prove zero custody exposure. IPO proceeds, CSR earmarks and lien FDs are not customer funds and are not shareholder-free cash.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is coordinated local sales execution and a useful channel-partner/developer network, not proprietary lending capital. FY25 repeat-client revenue of 44.05% supports relationship value. Against that, the top customer contributed 16.32% and the top ten 53.79%; Pune and Mumbai together were 98.78%. This concentration creates project and developer dependence and does not evidence a national distribution moat. No sufficiently quantified retention cohort, renewal pricing, exclusive network, switching-cost advantage or share trajectory was found to justify a strong moat score.

Primary peer disclosures challenge easy claims of uniqueness. Homesfy reported FY26 revenue ₹40.32 crore and PAT minus ₹20.49 crore; its marketing-heavy lead model and billed/unbilled bridge are not directly comparable to Justo's developer mandates. It demonstrates competitive difficulty, not Justo market-share superiority. Aurum's Q1FY27 distribution revenue ₹56 crore and segment profit ₹8 crore sit in a much wider technology/rental group; using whole-group valuation as a pure brokerage comparable would mislead. ANAROCK's official AI scale claims show that AI-assisted CP and sales infrastructure is available to competitors, although those claims are not audited. Software under development and stated network size do not alone prove durable excess economics. MOAT 4 reflects contestable differentiation, while acknowledging profitable relationships.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue rose from ₹10.0663 crore in FY21 to ₹91.7826 crore in FY26, a five-year 55.59% CAGR. The base is pandemic-affected and early in a company incorporated in 2019. The preselected more informative FY23–26 window grows from ₹70.4408 to ₹91.7826 crore at 9.22%; FY22–26 is separately disclosed at 32.05%. No additional small-base penalty is applied after choosing the mature window. The December 2025 Hustlewin acquihire added 25 professionals and four mandates; separate revenue is not quantified, so this is reported/economic fee growth, not a claim that every rupee is organic. Annual additions were ₹20.1162, ₹40.2583, minus ₹11.0580, ₹21.9691 and ₹10.4307 crore from FY22 through FY26.

A first-order gross/net check subtracts CP brokerage expense: ₹63.9779 crore in FY23 versus ₹83.3890 in FY26, 9.23% CAGR, the same REV band. This is not an independently audited net-fee segment. Management-reported property GMV rises from ₹2,133.36 crore to ₹2,630 crore, only 7.23% CAGR; FY23–25 sold units were 3,364, 2,634 and 2,839, while FY26 units are not verified. FY26 H1 revenue fell about 6.5% and H2 grew about 30.8%, a mixed recovery rather than four clean accelerating quarters. REV therefore starts and ends at 4 under the 5–<10% schedule. Neither a large TAM nor FY27 revenue guidance of ₹105–110 crore upgrades demonstrated growth.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There is an accessible service runway through deeper developer mandates, more CP throughput, additional cities, loan cross-sell and the Chestertons India subsidiary. Bottom-up scaling must mean more monetized property sales at stable net fee economics and collections, not simply a larger mandate GMV or technology budget. The company reported FY27 GMV guidance of ₹3,400–3,700 crore alongside revenue ₹105–110 crore and PAT ₹24–26 crore; these are management aspirations, not the forecast used to force an attractive return. Existing geographic access supports DUR 6, while funding and proven project returns remain separate tests.

Reinvestment is not costless: receivables, software development and people can consume substantial cash despite a service label. FY26 software under development reached ₹8.164 crore and no amortization is recognized until completion. The collection-adjusted FY23–26 capital proxy increased ₹83.7711 crore while proxy NOPAT rose ₹4.19745 crore, a weak 5.01% diagnostic versus an assumed 13–17% cost-of-capital range. However tax/provision treatment, changing service-fee presentation and software attribution prevent that ratio from being a reliable project/cohort return. CAP stays NS rather than promoting current ROE into reinvestment quality or asserting a proven below-cost cohort. GQS is incomplete; persistent poor cash conversion imposes the cap described in the audit, even though operating demand can grow.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Governance concern centers on repeated historical private-placement compliance failures under Section 42, including separate-bank and filing requirements. The company made a suo moto application; the FY26 secretarial report describes a ROC monetary penalty and appeal pending. Management describes technical shortcomings and strengthened processes. A primary-verified penalty amount and final appeal decision were not located, so neither is invented. Recurring late statutory-payment interest, ₹0.2454 crore in FY26 versus ₹0.4798 crore FY25, is a concrete control concern. Promoter ownership was 39.49% in September; director remuneration increased to ₹2.40 crore from ₹1.80 crore.

The group perimeter needs fair treatment. Justo Infotech Labs was acquired in August 2024 for nominal ₹1 lakh and is wholly owned; Chestertons India was incorporated in March 2026 and is wholly owned. A March-effective intragroup business transfer documented later used ₹9.50 crore OCPS consideration and generated a ₹0.3522 crore parent gain eliminated at group level. That is not external cash sale income or third-party dilution. Promise-versus-delivery evidence is mixed: IPO debt repayment is corroborated by actual debt notes; technology spending remains incomplete and aged; June monitoring reports no deviation with remaining purpose-bound funds; new mandates and partial AR recoveries are disclosed, but FY27 forecasts are not yet verified outcomes. GOV 5 and EXEC 5 acknowledge both substantive concerns and counterevidence without treating a KAM or consolidation difference as wrongdoing.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 revenue ₹91.7826 crore produced EBIT ₹27.2655 and PAT ₹19.2104, but CFO was minus ₹9.4137. The cash-flow bridge starts with PBT ₹26.0950 plus noncash/finance adjustments ₹3.1809, then minus ₹35.1707 working-capital absorption and ₹3.5189 taxes paid. Receivable cash absorption ₹38.7556 equals the ₹37.1312 balance increase plus ₹1.6244 bad-debt write-off; a write-off is not collection. Combined liability/provision movement reconciles after net-tax and retained ICD-interest reclassification, rather than implying tax was duplicated. FY23–26 CFO of minus ₹12.5731 against PAT ₹56.1691 and cash capex ₹11.5113 yields FCF proxy minus ₹24.0844. This FCF excludes separate nonoperating property purchases and is not an all-in cash-surplus measure.

March cash ₹23.1885 contains ₹19.1205 cheques; hard bank/physical cash less CSR is only ₹3.9035. Other FDs of ₹19.83 are under lien. FY25 cheques did clear subsequently, important counterevidence; FY26 clearance was not established. AR ₹86.5647 includes ₹9.6508 older than a year, yet is classified good. Subsequent standalone cohort reductions of ₹9.10 are attributed to management and cannot be substituted for a verified cash/cheque bridge. Debt is ₹15.2297, chiefly ₹14.8711 on demand; statutory and income-tax claims total ₹11.5705. Employee provisions ₹1.5700 stay in operating working capital, not deducted twice as debt; no separate closing accrued-interest amount is invented.

IPO gross proceeds ₹63.0047 less statutory cash issue costs ₹8.2284 give ₹54.7763 net. Monitoring's ₹6.84 ex-tax cost basis is different and the complete cost-tax-prepayment bridge remains open; neither cost is subtracted twice. June FD principal ₹5.68 is not all spare operating cash. The prospectus disclosed a historical ₹12 crore CC sanction with ₹7.4964 drawn at March 2025 and repo plus 2.80% pricing. The FY26 draw is already ₹14.8711; an updated limit/headroom was not located, so historical apparent headroom cannot be imported into October or used to allege a facility breach. Investment-property balance growth is bridged by ₹3.6469 current cash plus ₹1.3205 old advances. Historical statutory/restated PAT and FY22 CFO differences are preserved, with disclosed timing/classification explanations. Group PAT excludes the parent intragroup gain. These reconciliations support conditional reliability while cash availability and collection remain unresolved.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the secondary ₹82.90 price, market capitalization is ₹155.8366 crore, current-share FY26 EPS ₹10.2193, P/E 8.112 and P/B 1.233. Reported weighted diluted EPS ₹11.77 is not the correct denominator for today's entire share count. An indicative EV excluding unbanked cheques and restricted FDs is ₹167.1628 crore, 6.058 times FY26 EBITDA, but it combines a March balance with an October price and is not a claim about current net debt. All other income is excluded from operating EBIT. Nonoperating property recovery is separately haircutted, with no rental profit included in operating value and no extra value for software already supporting that profit.

The explicit model begins at March 2026, bridges to the October entry and ends at October 2031. It uses actual leap-year weights for partial periods, 25% corporate tax, retained operating cash equal to 5% of revenue, no dividends and no invented borrowing. Bear/base/bull growth, margins, collections, capex, debt repayment and exit multiples are fully specified below. Opening statutory/income-tax claims are paid immediately as a deliberately conservative stress, not as proof of current arrears or default. The 0%/2.5%/5% reserve and immediate-versus-end-FY27 tax sensitivities distinguish analytical conservatism from actual default; timing can remove modeled breaches without verifying current cash. A separate capped IPO-IT schedule credits eligible capex once: March ₹5.28 earmark, disclosed pre-entry ₹0.05 draw, then assumed eligible deployment capped at the remaining ₹5.23. A no-draw sensitivity avoids assuming unrestricted lien release. Required cash is subtracted with its sign, never erased with a zero floor.

Ordinary returns and entry prices are all null because current financeability is not verified; main non-rescue cases also breach required reserves before entry. The separate discounted-equity rescue and full-cheque-realization experiments are not ordinary targets. The rescue reverse solver validates finite funded endpoints and a bracket crossing before reporting approximately 3.94% constant growth for a 15% return under base assumptions. That apparently modest expectation still needs sustained margins, collections and hypothetical financing. P 5 recognizes an undemanding headline multiple without awarding R. Sensitivities cover 12/15/18% hurdles, 60/120 extra collection days, capex +3% of sales and 6/9/12 times EBIT. DCF is not forced; terminal-value share is not applicable to this explicit earnings-multiple method.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that the operating service is fictitious. It is that developer fees are real but slow or partly unrecoverable, channel relationships are contestable, technology absorbs cash before payback, and a small public company must recapitalize before shareholders can realize reported earnings. A property slowdown can reduce completed transactions and developer liquidity together. In that linked stress the model applies weaker revenue/margins, 390-day collections, a 15% opening AR write-off, heavier capex, one-year CC repayment and 50% property recovery. The write-off reduces opening working capital without pretending to be cash; software receives no separate value.

The conservative tax-timing assumption exacerbates the pre-entry gap and must not be described as an observed funding failure. Counterevidence is meaningful: FY25 cheques subsequently cleared, partial older-cohort collections were reported, IPO proceeds funded real business needs, the group remains profitable and property may recover value. Nonetheless, the separately funded rescue bear still produces a negative five-year shareholder return and material ownership dilution. A low P/E cannot prevent permanent loss if receivables require large haircuts or lenders withdraw demand funding while equity is unavailable. The thesis-break variable is cash collectible on usable terms, not only revenue growth. Supported evidence of cheque realization and adequate unrestricted resources would substantially change the bridge; a larger management mandate alone would not.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price gain requires 37.97% annualized over five years or 17.46% over ten; tenfold requires 58.49% or 25.89%. Holding the current share count fixed, fivefold equity value would be ₹779.18 crore and tenfold ₹1,558.37 crore. At a simple 25% EBIT margin and 9 times EBIT exit with static claims, the corresponding revenue levels are approximately ₹348.14 and ₹694.44 crore. These are scale requirements, not price targets or forecasts. They omit the additional funding and dilution needed to support such a business and therefore cannot prove feasibility.

The actual three-year reported revenue CAGR of 9.22% and GMV CAGR of 7.23% are far below the five-year operating scale requirements. Long-duration compounding could mathematically lower the annual hurdle, but it requires high net-fee retention, broader customers, much better cash conversion and attractive incremental economics, none of which is established at compounder quality. More software spending or headline property GMV cannot fill that evidentiary gap. The full annual scenarios and rescue dilution are the more informative shareholder tests; 5×/10× language should not displace them.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor the next published statements and specific disclosures, rather than treating reminders as verified new facts. First, reconcile the ₹19.1205 crore FY26 cheques to realized unrestricted bank cash and distinguish this from AR reductions; absence of clearance is not itself dishonour. Second, track the ₹86.5647 crore AR book, the ₹9.6508 crore over-one-year cohort and fresh bad debts; a further rise in aged balances with weak cash is adverse. Third, require cumulative CFO to turn positive and materially converge toward profits; one temporary supplier/tax delay is insufficient. Fourth, track each remaining IPO IT object and lien/earmark status against actual eligible expenditures, without reclassifying earmarked money as free cash.

Fifth, obtain demand-facility headroom, covenant/maturity terms and tax-payment timing in a conservative current resources bridge. Sixth, verify developer/customer and city concentration beyond FY25 and gross/net CP mix so demand is comparable. Seventh, compare FY27 management revenue/PAT/GMV guidance with actual sales, fees and collections rather than mandate values. Eighth, verify software completion, amortization start and attributable incremental earnings/cash returns. Ninth, resolve the ROC appeal and repeated statutory-payment controls. Tenth, acquire a complete official BSE 60-session ledger, current restrictions, spread and whole-lot depth before any implementation judgment. G3 can change when available resources cover credible stress; G4 can change when executable evidence supports the actual intended position.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification is Hold—unresolved, with a possible value/collection-recovery thesis rather than an established compounder. It cannot be ranked against fully evidenced companies using a fabricated midpoint. BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS; this is not equivalent to zero quality, a neutral score or a universal rejection. Compounder criteria are not met: moat and demonstrated revenue growth are 4, CAP is unresolved, CASH is 2 and funding/tradability gates remain open. A strong quoted operating margin is not a substitute for incremental return and cash realization.

At this price, the market does not mechanically demand spectacular growth, but whether shareholders can capture even fair-case earnings depends on assets turning into usable cash and avoiding adverse capital issuance. The current action category is further research/watch, not a purchase or ordinary target range. Necessary evidence is specific: subsequent cheque and receivable realization, actual unrestricted cash and funding terms, obligations timing, eligible IPO deployment, comparable fee economics and current whole-lot liquidity. A later lower price can improve the payoff only after those feasibility checks; it cannot repair a missing financing bridge. No trade, personal allocation recommendation or claimed investment certainty is made.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary issuer annual reports, the final prospectus, exchange-result mirrors, monitoring reports and aggregate shareholding support company facts. Official exchange security data supports identity, lot and shares; secondary price/trade series is explicitly limited. Peer claims are taken from first-party filings or an official company article and not silently promoted to audited market-share facts. Sources were retrieved after the cutoff, but only documents and observations dated on or before 20 October 2026 are used. Management's August deck has a date in its filename; the exact underlying YTD collection cutoff is not stated. The source register retains precise URLs, hashes when downloaded and locators. Original documents, OCR, images and individual shareholder identifiers are not part of the analytical backups.

The main judgmental assumptions are 25% future tax, 5% operating-cash reserve, scenario margins and DSO, an 11% cash interest rate, explicit debt repayment, capex ratios, assumed eligible restricted IT deployment, 6/9/12 times terminal EBIT and 50/70/85% nonoperating property recovery. These are not management promises. Immediate opening tax settlement is a stress bound, not a verified current cash call. Rescue uses a 30% issue discount and 5% fees and may be needed before entry; there is no evidence it is available or occurred. Open questions are current cash accessibility, FY26 cheque realization, full issue-cost tax/prepayment bridge, customer/mix evolution, software payback, final ROC status and official trading completeness. A source-safe reproduction verifies calculations from retained extracts, not fresh authentication of the original documents.

summary: Justo Realfintech is a real-estate sales and marketing services company, not a lender. Its profitable developer mandates, repeat relationships and relatively low earnings multiple are the positive case. The decisive contrary evidence is that accounting profit has not become operating cash: FY23–26 cumulative CFO was minus ₹12.57 crore against ₹56.17 crore PAT. At the ₹82.90 secondary observation, it is a conditional value/collection-recovery candidate, not a demonstrated growth compounder. The conclusion is Hold—unresolved, not an assertion of fraud or default. Current accessible funding and executable SME liquidity must be established before an ordinary return or investment ranking is defensible. Realization of FY26 cheques, collection discipline and actual incremental returns could change that assessment; a lower price alone cannot settle those questions.
